title: GeoJSON Viewer: Paste, Plot, Inspect
description: Plot GeoJSON points, lines and polygons on a local map with the GeoJSON Viewer — paste or drop, no upload, instant visual check. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a delivery-radius polygon pasted from an API response appears on the map in under a second — and the neighbourhood it accidentally covers is immediately, visibly obvious.
quick_answer: The GeoJSON Viewer plots pasted or dropped GeoJSON — points, lines and polygons — on a map in your browser, locally. Paste the text or drop the file and see your data's geography at once: the fastest possible answer to 'where does this file actually think things are?'

body.t: Your pipeline emits GeoJSON; the viewer is the smoke test. Wrong-hemisphere exports confess instantly. Structural doubts go to the
A contractor's boundary file, an open-data download, a colleague's attachment — see it before you agree it is what it claims to be.
If it plots here, your file is fine and your app has the bug. If it plots in the ocean off West Africa, the file's coordinates are swapped or defaulted — the classic 0,0 neighbourhood.
Sometimes the deliverable is one screenshot of the data on a map. The viewer produces it without a GIS project ever existing.

Data authored lat,lon instead of lon,lat plots mirrored into the wrong ocean — New York data surfaces off Somalia's latitude with longitude's sign games. One look diagnoses what an hour of code review might miss.

All seven RFC 7946 geometry types render — Points through GeometryCollections. A Feature with null geometry renders nothing, correctly: there is nothing to draw, and the properties still exist for the table tools.

popular_table.note: The viewer assumes RFC 7946: WGS84 longitude/latitude. Files in projected coordinates (metres) plot as garbage near the origin — recognisably, which is itself the diagnosis.

faq: All of them: Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon and GeometryCollection, as Features or bare geometries.
Select a feature from the list to inspect up to ten properties in a map popup.
Limits depend on browser memory and rendering performance. Large datasets may be slow or fail; no specific capacity is guaranteed.
The viewer draws a clear default style so the data reads immediately. Publication styling is a GIS or web-map-library task; this page answers 'where is it?'
